# Wizard: retry offered for deterministic BMAD setup failures

## What happened

During first-run wizard BMAD onboarding (v1.0.0), a repo with a pre-existing broken BMAD state
produced:

```
> BMAD setup for RightTenantryAgents failed: BMAD manifest declares missing or unsafe module directory: /Users/moses/code/RightTenancy.../_bmad/core
Retry or skip this repo? [retry/skip]:
```

Every `retry` re-runs the same deterministic check against unchanged repo state and fails
identically — the user retried 3+ times before skipping. (Observed sibling class: "existing BMAD
install lacks selected runtime binding(s)" also cannot succeed via retry.)

## Why it's wrong

`retry` only makes sense for transient failures (network, tool download). These failures are
deterministic state checks — retry cannot change the outcome and just loops the user.

## Desired behavior

- Classify BMAD setup failures: transient → offer retry/skip; deterministic (missing/unsafe module
  dir, manifest/binding mismatch) → skip-only, with the actionable escape hatch in the prompt
  (e.g. "run `npx bmad-method install` in the repo to deliberately update the install").

## Acceptance

- A repo whose manifest declares a missing/unsafe module dir yields a skip-only prompt (no retry).
- The same for the binding-mismatch class.
- Prompt text names the deliberate-fix path.
title: Wizard: retry offered for deterministic BMAD setup failures
